name: Chlorpromazine
executiveSummary: Phenothiazine antipsychotic. Adult agitation: **25–50 mg IM/IV**; psychosis PO **200–800 mg/day**. Antiemetic: **10–25 mg** every 4–6 h. Pediatrics >6 months: **0.5–1 mg/kg/dose**. Diluted IV ≤**0.5 mg/min**.
indications:
## Indications

- Psychomotor agitation / acute psychosis.
- Refractory nausea/vomiting; intractable hiccups; selected chorea.

## Precautions

- Postural hypotension, QT, extrapyramidal symptoms, neuroleptic malignant syndrome.
- IV: dilute to **1 mg/mL** in NS; **≤0.5 mg/min**. Avoid skin contact with solution (dermatitis).
- Not in CNS coma; caution in epilepsy, glaucoma, urinary retention.

> Correct name: **chlorpromazine**.

adulto.presentation: Tabs 25–100 mg; IM ampoule 5 mg/mL; IV 25 mg/mL.
adulto.dose: Agitation: **25 mg IM/IV**; repeat in 1–4 h (orient. max **400 mg**/dose at extremes; usual cumulative **300–800 mg/day**). Psychosis PO: start **25–50 mg**; usual **200 mg/day** (range **30–800 mg/day**). Antiemetic: **10–25 mg PO** or **25–50 mg IM/IV** every 4–6 h.
adulto.administration: PO. Deep IM. IV only diluted and slow.
adulto.notes: Monitor BP. Interactions: propranolol, antacids, valproate.

pediatrico.dose: >6 months: **0.5–1 mg/kg/dose** every 4–6 h. Max IM/IV: <5 years **40 mg/day**; 5–12 years **75 mg/day**.

stability:
## Stability

- IV dilution: per card (some institutional cards ~7 days reconstituted — verify).
adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Sedation, hypotension, anticholinergic effects, extrapyramidal symptoms, QT/arrhythmias, hyperprolactinemia, photosensitivity, rare agranulocytosis.
